title: Helicity-Defined Analog Memory in Chiral Perovskites Featured by Korea University
shortDescription: Korea University highlighted a co-first-author Advanced Materials study that stores optical handedness as persistent analog conductance states.
detailText: Min Jong Lee and Hyoungwook Cho contributed equally as first authors. The study demonstrated 72 distinguishable conductance states retained for 10⁶ s and evaluated a 7×7 device array. Read-noise analysis estimated a state capacity of 72.3; this estimate is distinct from the 72 experimentally demonstrated states.
thumbnailAlt: Conceptual artwork of circularly polarized light interacting with a layered chiral perovskite; not an experimental image
